ticket.summary: Water pouring through dining room ceiling light fixture from suspected upstairs bathroom leak; customer located and closed house main in garage, on-call dispatch requested.
mitigation_advice: Shut off the house main - checked basement, then garage/meter box; found wheel valve by water heater in garage and closed it clockwise [PB-02]
Open the lowest cold tap in the house to drain pressure from the lines [PB-03]
Stay out from under the sagging water-logged ceiling and away from the soaked light fixture; do not operate it [PB-08]
ticket.customer_message: Great work! Water will keep dripping a few minutes as the upstairs pipes drain - open the lowest cold tap to bleed pressure [PB-03]; if it's still pouring after ~10 min the main isn't fully closed, tighten it more. Keep everyone out from under the ceiling and don't touch the soaked light fixture or its switch [PB-08]. I'm paging the on-call plumber now - they'll call you at 555-0104 with an ETA. After-hours dispatch is $150 (EMERG-CALLOUT); repair costs are quoted after they see the source.
